question.problem: Starting with the standard Maclaurin expansion for $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x),$ find the first three non-zero terms of the series expansion for $\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(1-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x.$
question.worked_solution:
The series expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)$ is

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)=x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-⋯\,.
$$

Replacing $x$ with $-{x}^{2}$ in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-{x}^{2}) & =(-{x}^{2})-\frac{1}{2}(-{x}^{2})^{2}+\frac{1}{3}(-{x}^{2})^{3}-⋯ \\  & =-{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{6}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, integrating with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(1-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & =\int (-{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{6}-⋯)\text{d}x \\  & =C-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{10}-\frac{{x}^{7}}{21}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
